card.name: Hedging words before harm descriptions
card.fires_on: Qualifier words such as "potentially" or "sometimes" placed just before a harmful or severe term, most often in overdose text about fatal liver damage. It also fires weakly on other verbs or commas leading into a claim.

modes.label: Potentially before fatal
modes.description: The word "potentially" directly before "fatal" in acetaminophen overdose warnings.
modes.example: In acute acetaminophen overdosage, dose-dependent,<< potentially>> fatal hepatic necrosis is the most

modes.label: Other qualifiers and lead-ins
modes.description: Words like "sometimes", "near" or "contained" that lead into a toxic or harmful amount or thing.
modes.example: some 40 million people subsequently were exposed to toxic levels of arsenic,<< sometimes>> exceeding the World Health Organization (WHO)

card.writes: It pushes toward superlative and praise words like "world-class" and "powerful" and away from technical nouns, so the pattern is unclear.
card.plain: It marks the hedge word right before a statement about something serious or harmful, like "potentially fatal".
